conventions.convention: Matrix dimensions are positive. Coordinate labels 1,…,n correspond to library indices 0,…,n−1; restrictions h_S are zero-extended vectors and complements are relative to [n].
Strict NSP of order s, with 1≤s≤n, tests every nonzero exact kernel vector and every support of size at most s, including the empty support. A zero kernel satisfies it vacuously.
The uniform margin uses one constant ρ∈(0,1) for all admissible supports and all exact kernel vectors, including zero; it asserts no estimate for Ah≠0.
The Gaussian example assumes full AC, independent coordinates with variance σ²/n, integers n≥1, d≥2 and 1≤s≤d/2, and Borel estimators. Its loss is unnormalized squared Euclidean error.

load_bearing.statement: For m,n≥1 and 1≤s≤n, A satisfies strict NSP of order s if ‖h_S‖₁<‖h_{Sᶜ}‖₁ for every nonzero h∈ker A and every S⊆[n] with |S|≤s.
Let m,n≥1, 1≤s≤n, and A∈R^{m×n} satisfy strict NSP of order s. Every x†∈Rⁿ with at most s nonzero coordinates is the unique minimizer of ∑|z_j| subject to Az=Ax†.
For m,n≥1, 1≤s≤n and A∈R^{m×n} satisfying the strict nullspace inequalities, there exists ρ∈(0,1) such that ∑_{j∈S}|h_j|≤ρ∑_{j∉S}|h_j| for every h with Ah=0 and every S⊆[n] with |S|≤s.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite real matrices and their zero-based row and column indices.
Matrix multiplication and the identity matrix in the Gaussian identity-design example.
The finite-dimensional one-norm and two-norm formulas.
Triangle inequality, separation, and absolute homogeneity.
Norm properties and identification of the Euclidean norm-induced metric with d₂ for positive dimensions.
Linearity of finite matrix action, disjoint-support norm decomposition, monotonicity, and evaluation of identity-matrix sums.
Identification of a matrix row functional with its Euclidean inner product.
Continuity of the one-norm and the reverse triangle inequality in the uniform-margin argument.
Taking the maximum over the finite nonempty family of admissible supports.
Passing between squared and unsquared Euclidean projection bounds.
Continuity estimates for matrix row functionals.
Choice-free compactness of the nonempty normalized kernel and attainment of continuous ratio maxima.
The explicit full-AC hypothesis inherited by the Gaussian minimax example.
The risk lower bound σ²s log(ed/s)/(200000n), with matching parameter, noise, sparsity, AC and Borel-estimator hypotheses.
